emails.subject: Blood Pressure Checks at DHM Digital
emails.body: A blood pressure check measures the force of blood against your artery walls as your heart beats and rests. The result is two numbers — systolic over diastolic — recorded in millimetres of mercury (mmHg). DHM Digital's blood pressure checks service helps identify raised readings early, when many people still feel completely well. The pharmacist measures your blood pressure using a validated device, explains your result, and arranges the next step. Call 059) 0 0 60 (Sheffield).

emails.subject: Your Blood Pressure Checks appointment at DHM Digital
emails.body: Blood Pressure Checks — Contact DHM Digital to ask whether you can walk in or need to book. When you arrive, the team will confirm whether the service is suitable for you and explain what will happen. You will be seen in a private consultation area. The pharmacist or trained pharmacy staff will ask about your health history, current medicines, and any symptoms. They will check whether you are eligible for the NHS service and explain how your result will be shared with your GP. Call 059) 0 0 60 (Sheffield).

emails.subject: What to expect from Blood Pressure Checks at DHM Digital
emails.body: Blood Pressure Checks — If your reading is within the normal range — No further action is usually needed immediately. You will be advised when to have your blood pressure checked again — typically around every five years, or sooner if you are close to the upper limit or have other health factors such as diabetes. If your reading is raised — This does not mean you have been diagnosed with high blood pressure. DHM Digital will offer ABPM where the NHS service applies, so your blood pressure can be measured across a full day rather than at a single moment. If a device is available, fitting may happen the same day or within a few days. Call 059) 0 0 60 (Sheffield).

emails.subject: When to seek other care — DHM Digital
emails.body: Blood Pressure Checks — From DHM Digital — Blood pressure screening is not for emergencies. Call 999 or go to A&E for chest pain, suspected stroke, severe breathing difficulty, collapse, sudden confusion, or any life-threatening symptom — regardless of what a blood pressure reading shows. Seek same-day medical review if your clinic reading is 180/120 or higher (even without symptoms), if ABPM shows a very high average, if the device detects an irregular pulse that is not already known and investigated, or if your reading is low and you experience regular fainting, falls, or daily fear of fainting. Call 999 immediately if a very high reading is accompanied by chest pain, severe headache with neurological symptoms, new confusion, signs of heart failure, or acute kidney problems. The NHS pharmacy service is not appropriate when you need emergency care, when you require daily blood pressure monitoring over a set period, when you are pregnant and need maternity blood pressure assessment, or when you fall outside the service eligibility criteria without a GP referral. Call 059) 0 0 60 (Sheffield).
